SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. At what age can a person legally marry in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 12 years
   B. 14 years
   C. 16 years
   D. 18 years

2. Which is a way to promote child rights in school? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring children with problems
   B. Making posters and songs on child protection
   C. Hiding problems
   D. Bullying

3. Which of these can you call for help in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A shop
   B. The child helpline 116
   C. A cinema
   D. A bakery

4. What is child trafficking? (1 mark)
   A. Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them
   B. Taking children on a picnic
   C. Adopting children legally
   D. Taking children to school

5. How often are general elections held in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Every five years
   B. Every month
   C. Every year
   D. Every ten years

6. Which of these is a democratic process in school? (1 mark)
   A. Punishing pupils who speak
   B. Ignoring pupils' ideas
   C. Electing a class monitor by voting
   D. A bully choosing leaders

7. At what age can a Kenyan vote in national elections? (1 mark)
   A. 10 years
   B. 15 years
   C. 18 years
   D. 12 years

8. What is campaigning? (1 mark)
   A. Counting votes
   B. Throwing away ballots
   C. Telling voters why they should choose you
   D. Announcing results

9. Why should voting be secret? (1 mark)
   A. So that votes are lost
   B. So that the winner is hidden
   C. So that nobody can force how you vote
   D. So that nobody counts

10. Who takes over when the president of the Children's Government is absent? (1 mark)
   A. The visitor
   B. The cook
   C. The parent
   D. The deputy president

11. What is the meaning of composition of a group? (1 mark)
   A. The song of the group
   B. The colour of the group
   C. The size of the room
   D. The people or parts that make up the group

12. Which item usually comes first on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Reports
   B. Closing remarks
   C. Opening prayer or song
   D. Suggestions

13. Which is the right way to make a complaint? (1 mark)
   A. By shouting in class
   B. Through your class representative
   C. By fighting
   D. By spreading rumours

14. Which duty belongs to a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. Selling goods
   B. Making laws
   C. Repairing cars
   D. Leading prayers and teaching values

15. Which action shows good leadership? (1 mark)
   A. Hiding the food
   B. Giving only to friends
   C. Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   D. Keeping all the food

16. Who leads a location and is appointed by the national government? (1 mark)
   A. Pastor
   B. Village poet
   C. Chief
   D. Clan elder

17. What is devolution? (1 mark)
   A. Ending the government
   B. Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments
   C. Keeping all power in one place
   D. A kind of tax

18. Which law created county governments in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A market rule
   B. A church rule
   C. The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   D. A school rule

19. Which of these is a county government service? (1 mark)
   A. Running the army
   B. Running county health centres
   C. Defending the country
   D. Issuing passports

20. What is public participation? (1 mark)
   A. Citizens leaving
   B. Citizens hiding
   C. Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   D. Citizens breaking laws

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how citizens can support the county government. (4 marks)

22. Explain the difference between a chief and a clan elder. (3 marks)

23. Describe the duties of ward and village administrators. (4 marks)

24. State three duties of the governor. (3 marks)

25. Explain why a Children's Government should not punish pupils. (3 marks)

26. Describe how a class can invite a resource person to talk about leadership. (4 marks)

27. Explain what a Children's Government is. (2 marks)

28. What is a majority? (2 marks)

29. State three duties of clan elders. (3 marks)

30. Explain why a ballot should be secret. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 18 years
   The law says a person must be 18 to marry.

2. B — Making posters and songs on child protection
   Awareness helps protect children.

3. B — The child helpline 116
   Childline Kenya can be reached on 116.

4. A — Taking children away by trick or force to make money from them
   Trafficking is a crime.

5. A — Every five years
   Kenya holds general elections every five years.

6. C — Electing a class monitor by voting
   Voting gives everyone a say.

7. C — 18 years
   Adults aged 18 and above can vote.

8. C — Telling voters why they should choose you
   Candidates campaign before elections.

9. C — So that nobody can force how you vote
   Secret voting protects free choice.

10. D — The deputy president
   The deputy helps and takes over.

11. D — The people or parts that make up the group
   Composition means the members that make up a group.

12. C — Opening prayer or song
   Meetings begin with an opening.

13. B — Through your class representative
   Use proper channels.

14. D — Leading prayers and teaching values
   Religious leaders lead worship.

15. C — Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   Fairness and honesty are good leadership.

16. C — Chief
   A chief leads a location.

17. B — Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments
   Devolution moves some power to counties.

18. C — The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   The 2010 Constitution created counties.

19. B — Running county health centres
   Health centres are a county responsibility.

20. C — Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   People take part in decisions.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Attend public meetings, vote, pay fees and taxes, and take care of public property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: A chief is appointed by the national government to lead a location. A clan elder is respected by a clan for age and wisdom and keeps customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: They bring county services close to people, pass on information, help organise public meetings, and take the community's needs to county leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lead the county executive, present the budget and plans, and represent the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Only teachers decide on discipline, pupil leaders may be unfair, and serious problems must be reported to teachers.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write a polite invitation, state the topic, give the date and time, and thank the visitor after the talk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a group of pupils elected by their classmates to help run the school and speak for pupils, guided by a teacher.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for elected pupils, 1 mark for helping and speaking for pupils.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: The larger number of votes, more than any other choice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for larger number, 1 mark for votes.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep customs, settle disputes and advise at ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: So that nobody can force or influence how a person votes, so the choice is free.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.
